info.title: Smart Lab Portal
info.description:
Smart Laboratory Management Portal.

Booking, time-bound QR credentials, laboratory maintenance, and the audit trail for the physical two-factor access-control system. The backend authorizes and records; the ESP32 master is the only thing that opens a door.

get.description: firstname.lastname from a name (the sign-up and Add user forms pre-fill it).

post.description:
Admin-only: create an account with any role (student, lab staff, admin)
and, optionally, its fingerprint/RFID subject. Public sign-up (below)
can only ever create an un-enrolled student.

get.description: What the login page needs to show (or hide) the sign-up form.

post.description:
Self-service sign-up. Always creates a STUDENT. With
AUTO_ASSIGN_AUTH_SUBJECT it gets the next door identity (USERn), which
opens nothing until staff enrol that person's fingerprint/face under the
same number. Admins are notified of every new account.

get.description: What this person still needs before a lab door will open for them.

schema.title: Response List Labs Api Labs Get

get.description:
Everything the laboratory catalogue shows, in one request, computed from
live rows: occupancy from open sessions, availability from the booking
table, controller state from heartbeats, issue counts from reports.

schema.title: Response Labs Overview Api Labs Overview Get

get.description:
Every lab that has an environment node, in one request: the overview
used to ask once per lab (11 requests, each re-checking every device).

Lab Health Score per lab (app/services/health_score.py): 0-100 + every part with its evidence; parts with no
data are left out and reported as coverage. Advisory - it ranks attention, it does not certify safety.

ADVISORY emergency headcount (priority N): who the DOOR record says is inside (named, from badge/finger/QR
entries without an exit) next to how many people the lab's cameras see now (a count, never names; two cameras
can see the same person, so the larger single-camera count is shown, not the sum). For a roll call at the
assembly point - not proof that anybody left or is still inside.

Smoke / flame alarms still open in any lab, and evacuation alarms switched
on in the Emergency tab - what the portal's full-screen alarm shows on a
page opened after the alarm started.

Latest environment reading per metric, each with its quality
(VALID / STALE / MISSING / DEVICE_OFFLINE / OUT_OF_RANGE).

Reserved intervals in [start, end), for the booking picker.

A student must see that 14:00-16:00 is taken without learning by whom -
so identity is returned only for the caller's own bookings or to staff.
Before this endpoint the picker read the student's own booking list,
which never contains anyone else's reservation, so taken hours showed as
free until the server refused the booking.

schema.title: Response Lab Availability Api Labs  Lab Id  Availability Get

get.description:
The lab's event timeline. Staff see all of it; a student sees only their
own events here, the same rule /access-events applies - the lab page is
not a way around it.

schema.title: Response Lab Activity Api Labs  Lab Id  Activity Get

get.description: Open problems in a lab: titles and states, never who reported them.

schema.title: Response Lab Issues Api Labs  Lab Id  Issues Get

get.description:
Returns whatever real readings exist - which is an empty list until a
sensor node is actually deployed. Nothing here fabricates values.

schema.title: Response Lab Sensors Api Labs  Lab Id  Sensors Get

get.description: Whole-lab time slider: the lab at time t, rebuilt from recorded history only (services/lab_at.py).

schema.title: Response List Bookings Api Bookings Get

get.description: What can be chosen for this lab and window (reserved items are marked).

Render the booking's door credential.

How it is drawn, and why every issued token is readable by the door, is
in app/services/qr.py.

When this booking was ACTUALLY used.

A booking of 14:00-16:00 with an entry at 14:16 is two different facts,
and a laboratory record that only stores the first one cannot answer who
was in the room when something happened.

schema.title: Response Booking Sessions Api Bookings  Booking Id  Sessions Get

get.description:
One booking, end to end: the reservation, the credential, every step at
the door, and the resulting session - the record needed to demonstrate
the physical flow and to reconstruct it afterwards.

post.description:
Step 1 for a booking QR.

Returns the canonical identity on success. The master then requires a
biometric that matches THIS identity before it unlocks anything.

Generic event sink for the master: biometric attempts, door transitions,
identity mismatches, exits. The master fires these and does not wait on
them, so a slow or absent portal never delays the door.

The master reports that it HAS granted access. This opens an occupancy
session; it does not authorize anything.

Device liveness and door state. Auto-registers an unknown device against
its lab so a freshly flashed board appears in the admin view without
manual setup.

Environmental readings from a sensor node (temperature, humidity, and
the hazard states smoke / flame / water_leak / emergency, plus motion).
Stored as reported with the server's UTC time; nothing is interpolated.
A hazard state raises (or clears) its alert at once - see
services/environment.py.

get.description:
The access timeline.

Staff and admins see everything. A STUDENT may read this too, but only
their own events - which is what makes the "your recent access" panel on
the student dashboard work at all.

The scoping is forced server-side rather than trusted from the query
string: a student who asks for somebody else's user_id is silently
narrowed back to themselves instead of being refused, because refusing
would leak whether that other user has any events.

schema.title: Response Access Events Api Access Events Get

get.description: Every occupancy session - entry, door cycle, and how it ended.

schema.title: Response Access Sessions Api Access Sessions Get

get.description:
The session a moment belongs to: the latest session of this person in
this lab that had started by `at` (plus a short margin, because the grant
is reported just after the biometric). Lets any access event link to its
session. Students may only look themselves up.

One visit, end to end: the booking (if any), step 1 and its identity,
step 2 and its identity, the grant, the door cycle, and an exit only if
one was recorded. Works for RFID entries with no booking too.

schema.title: Response List Users Api Users Get

get.description: The door identity the next account would get (USERn = fingerprint slot n).

post.description:
Remove a person from use - their history stays (bookings, door entries,
camera events are the lab's records): the account is disabled, every RFID
card and personal door QR revoked. Re-enable with 'Account active'.

get.description: The person's active cards (UIDs are identifiers, not secrets).

Liveness is recomputed on read: a device that stops sending heartbeats
never gets a chance to mark itself offline. Staff only - the list
includes network addresses.

schema.title: Response List Devices Api Devices Get

post.description:
Give one device its own key (shown once; only its hash is kept). A
device using it may report only as itself. Issuing again replaces it.

schema.title: Response List Assets Api Assets Get

get.description:
The equipment's record: where it is, who has it, when it was last
inspected, when maintenance is due, and everything that went wrong.

post.description: Record an inspection now, and optionally when the next one is due.

schema.title: Response List Alerts Api Alerts Get

get.description:
CSV of the audit trail, resolved to names rather than foreign keys, so it
can go straight into a thesis appendix or a spreadsheet.

Daily grant/deny counts per lab. Real aggregates over real rows - if
nothing has happened, the series is empty rather than padded.

Every aggregate the reports page draws, from real rows only. A section
with nothing behind it comes back empty and the page says "not enough
data yet" - nothing is interpolated, smoothed or sampled.

Hours are returned in UTC; the browser shifts them to local time.

put.description:
Set someone's password: administrators for anyone, lab staff for
students. Takes effect at the next sign-in; the audit log records who and
whose, never the password.

schema.title: Response List Issues Api Issues Get
Response Upload Photos Api Issues  Issue Id  Photos Post
Response List Photos Api Issues  Issue Id  Photos Get

get.description:
Streams the stored image. Authenticated like every other route: the
photos can show the inside of a laboratory, so they are not public files.

schema.title: Response List Notifications Api Notifications Get

get.description:
The Notifications page: one page of the caller's notifications with
the tab counts and the kinds present, newest first.
Read-only: configuration comes from the environment, not the browser.
The provenance new records get (a RUNNING experiment overrides it).

put.description: Administrators only. Affects NEW records only - history keeps its provenance.

get.description:
Every part of the lab system. Network services come from the background monitor's cache
(app/services/health_monitor.py) - this request never waits on a probe.
The System Health page: services + devices, data-source freshness, backups, a summary.
Pull feed over the outbox, in commit order. Resume from `next_after`.

parameters.name: after

schema.description: sequence of the last event already processed
schema.title: After

parameters.description: sequence of the last event already processed

post.description: The same reminder the portal raises itself - at most once per booking.

get.description: AI-written weekly summary for the n8n weekly report. Optional.
Robotics Lab watch rules (n8n workflows 13-22): notification items.

Workflow 23: a lab's emergency now, whether its door controller has
applied it, and one ready notice per person inside (they are told what
to do - leave, stay, the admin's message). Read-only.

post.description: A workflow reports that it ran - the Operations Center shows it.

get.description:
Every subsystem (door, environment, robots, consumables, cameras, PCs, automation, alerts):
daily series, totals and the freshness of each data source. Real tables only. Shared 20 s (app/core/ttl.py).
The shared KPI catalogue: id, definition, unit, source table, kind.
Typical week, recent days and environment. No per-person data.
The caller's own bookings only - never anyone else's.
Recorded rows as CSV, for spreadsheets and the thesis appendix.

Rules, sensor-fault checks and statistical baselines on the real measurements (no ML - see ml_status).
Cached 60 s: the scan reads ~25k readings (~0.9 s) and sensors report at most once a minute.

post.description: Raise finding #index of the current scan as an incident (once per day per device/metric/kind).

get.description: The official ranking. Deterministic - works without AI.

Weekly or monthly management report (no AI needed): figures, the
previous period, equipment use, repeated problems with recommendations.
The read-only lab tools with typed input schemas (what tools/mcp_server/server.py exposes over MCP).

post.description: One validated, audited, time-limited read-only tool call. Refusals and timeouts come back as status, not 500.

get.description:
One frame from the door camera, for the live preview while enrolling. First the frame the
camera already sent to the face server (no extra work for the camera, which is also busy with
the door); the camera's own /snapshot only when the face server has no fresh frame.

post.description: The camera takes one frame and hands it to the face server as a sample.

Start automatic capture: the face server keeps every steady, sharp, new-looking frame of
this person from the door camera's normal stream until `target` samples are saved.

Stop using this person's saved face samples (bad / few photos): the
face server moves them to its archive (kept, not deleted). Capture new
ones, then Finish.
Retrain the face server with the new samples and mark Face ID done.

get.description: The controller asks, while idle, whether a request is waiting for it.
Every submission waiting for review, oldest first (Users & roles).
The person or staff only; never public - these are photos of a face.

post.description: Not usable as they are: the person is asked to send new photos.
Refused: the person must come to the lab staff to be enrolled in person.
Stable masses from a bin node. Replies with what the LCD shows.
A physical count next to the current estimate: estimation error data.

Staff take an item out of the bin FOR a person (e.g. their booking has
ended). Same bin path: the lid opens and the weight confirms the take.

Staff record that a checked-out item is back (it came back without the
bin - bin fault, booking over). Logged as a STAFF return, never by the bin.

get.description:
Tagged items of a lab's smart bin. Who holds an item: staff see the
name, the holder sees "you", everyone else only that it is out.
The most recent tag a bin node scanned that no item has.

put.description: The item's mass for the bin's weight check (None = learn it again).

post.description: A tag at the bin. Replies with what the node does and shows.

After OPEN_FOR_RETURN: the lid cycle finished. The return is recorded
only if the lid opened (the item could go in) - it is never assumed.

After OPEN_LID for a checkout: the bin weighed before and after.
About one item less = the selected item is CHECKED_OUT to the person.
A settled weight change with no request running: nobody explained it.

get.description:
Robots + PCs with their current session. A fixed number of queries whatever the number of devices
(2026-10-26: was ~6 per device, and "running today" read every session the device ever had).
Asset Administration Shell (V3.0 JSON) of every registered asset - read-only export (app/services/aas.py).

post.description:
Called by the web app right after an admin signs in. The admin becomes the master; the lab PC
they sit at becomes the master PC only with a valid agent proof.

get.description: Who the master is now: the admin who signed in last, their device, and their lab PC (if any).

put.description: Mark (or unmark) a PC as the lab engineer's master PC.

post.description:
tools/lan_presence (on the lab laptop): which lab PCs answer on the LAN right now, by MAC
address - no agent needed on the PC. One PC's own key must not speak for the others, so only
the lab's shared device key is accepted. A PC seen for the first time gets its device row
(like the agent's first report); connects / disconnects are audited.

get.description:
For tools/lan_presence: every lab PC whose agent has reported its MAC address(es), so a new PC
is checked on the LAN without anyone typing its MAC (2026-10-21). Shared lab key only.

The PC agent asks every ~2 s: mode, whether staff are watching, and
one waiting message. Cheap on purpose (nothing is written unless a
message is handed over).

post.description:
One JPEG of the PC's screen, accepted only while staff are watching.
2026-11-04 lab: this async handler used a blocking DB session on the event loop; 13 PCs x 2 frames/s
(screen wall) froze the whole backend. The PC id now comes from the cached lookup, off the loop.

get.description: Latest frame, or 204 while the agent has not sent one yet.

post.description: Close the messages open on this PC and cancel one not delivered yet.
Admin shares their screen with the students' PCs (and anyone signed in on /share).

get.description: One-time nonce for the PC proof (as at the admin's sign-in): which lab PC the student sits at.

post.description:
A student asks to share their lab PC's screen. Only a PC whose agent proves itself can present
(its agent captures - the lab PCs' browsers run on plain http, where a page may not capture).
The presenting student ends their own share.
A frame captured in the presenting admin's browser.

A frame from the PC that presents: the admin's master PC, or a student's PC an admin accepted.
The DB lookup runs in the thread pool (never on the event loop - see pc_frame).

get.description:
Latest presented frame for anyone signed in (students watch on /share); 204 = none yet,
410 = sharing has ENDED (the viewer clears the picture at once instead of showing the last frame
until its next status check - "stop does not stop immediately", 2026-10-21).

post.description:
First start of the agent from the flash-drive kit: the kit's enrollment code -> this PC's own key. The same
PC_<computer name> keeps its one row (its name and history stay, the old key stops working), so running the
installer again never makes a duplicate card. Every enrollment is in the audit log.

get.description:
The signed agent update (tools/pc_agent/make_bundle.py). Public code, no secrets: the signature, checked on
the PC against a public key it already holds, is what makes it trustworthy.

The idle PC agent waits here instead of polling every second: answers {"changed": true} as soon
as something for this PC changes (a viewer opens or changes monitor/quality, a share starts or stops,
an action / message / mode / master change), else {"changed": false} after `timeout`. Memory only -
no database work and no worker thread while waiting; the agent then calls /pc/poll as before.

post.description:
The camera matched its moved view to the room and reports where each
box went. Each box is moved and relearns its normal look; boxes that left
the picture are left as they were. In the audit log (no person: the camera).

get.description: The latest frame (annotated, or raw for drawing boxes). 204 = none.

Why each person in view has (or has not) a name: state, confidence and
the evidence behind it, plus recent identity decisions. Staff only; names,
scores and times - never face data.

Equipment the detector finds in the picture now (monitors, laptops) as
boxes to add, numbered after the boxes already saved. An item a saved box
already sits on (overlap > 0.6) is skipped. An item a saved box only
partly covers - the box is off its item, e.g. after the camera turned -
is offered as "move that box here" (replaces = its id; staff can pick
another box or a new one instead). Nothing is saved until staff add them.

post.description: The item's new position/look is fine: the camera relearns it.

get.description: Training pictures for the robot detector, kept on the laptop.

post.description: A link to play / download one recording, valid for 10 minutes.

get.description:
Streams one recording (with Range, so the player can seek). The signed
link IS the permission: an administrator asked for it minutes ago.

Every signed-in user (any role): the labs with an emergency message or
alarm right now - what a page opened after it was set shows and reads aloud.

Polled every second by the door controller. Read-mostly: it writes
only when a timed state has just run out.

Advisory safety triage (services/safety_triage.py): what to look at first, ranked, with evidence and ages.
Read-only; never actuates anything.

Proactive suggestions (services/proactive.py): CONFIRMED findings and POSSIBLE anomalies with evidence and
timestamps, de-duplicated; recomputed only when the data changed (at most once a minute), not per request.

All experiments, or one lab's: those run on a device of that lab
(experiments have no lab column; the device says where it ran).
Recent completed movements that carry their recorded path (3D replay).
One movement's recorded joint path: t (s from its start) and q (rad, J1..J6).

post.description:
HOME = the pose the robot is in NOW (the engineer put it there). Needs
fresh telemetry and a still robot. A new version; older ones are kept.

Global STOP: any staff member, no ownership needed, whoever started the motion. Latches
until an administrator runs the recovery. A software stop - not a safety-rated E-stop.
Any staff member cancels the automatic Home countdown (the idle clock restarts). Sends nothing to a robot.

get.description:
The stop-relay ESP32 asks every 200 ms. Only that device's OWN key (not the shared door key).
STOP whenever the portal's STOP latch for the robot is set; the answer never depends on the browser.

post.description:
Deliberate recovery after STOP (administrator, arm reported still). Restarts nothing.
With the hardware stop relay: refused while a program is still running / paused (closing the safeguard input
would let it carry on); the UR agent's own latch is cleared too.
Streams the agent's events (NDJSON): meta, step, sources, token, done.

get.description: Newest version of each named setup.

post.description: SIMULATION only: the consequences of `node` failing now. Nothing is changed.
Accept a deviation with a reason and an optional expiry. It stays visible; the baseline is not changed.
Re-run the read-only health checks now (policy: health.recheck = allowed). Bounded by their timeouts.

get.description:
The thesis evaluation (priority B): measured before/after results with their conditions and the script or
document that produced them; unmeasured items are listed as such (app/data/evaluation.json).

Everything the palette can find, with the words that make it relevant. `keys` = what the item
is called (code, tag, uid); `words` = what it is (type and subject words); `lab` = where it is.

Alert quality: grouped share, repeat rows, noisy devices and conditions, time to acknowledge /
resolve, reopen (recurrence), storms. Read-only.

schema.title: Response Reports Api Uiperf Reports Get

get.description:
The printable marker of a registered asset (exact text = its record key). style=pack (default): the owner's
marker pack - category motif in recoloured real modules (services/marker_pack.py); style=shape: the object-
shaped variant (marker_shapes.py). qr_only=1: the code alone. Every marker is decoded back before serving.
Vector QR of a registered asset (responsive previews; the PNG card is for printing).
All markers of one kind for the markers page in one response (registry read once, artwork cached).
Every marker of one kind on A4 sheets (the pack's 2 x 4 card layout, 300 dpi).
QR of a portal address (desktop -> phone handoff). https:// portal paths only - not a general QR maker.

post.description:
Person boxes for one phone frame. The camera service answers 429 while it is busy with another phone frame
(one at a time - the fixed cameras keep priority); the phone then simply sends its NEXT frame.

One target-aware question from the live camera (typed or spoken). The target is resolved on the server
from the marker code / face ticket; intents with live data are answered exactly and instantly; anything
else goes to the local model with that live data as explicit context.

get.description: Which registered enclosures have reference photos yet (data/asset_refs/manifest.json).

post.description:
One phone frame -> which enclosure it LOOKS like (PROBABLE / AMBIGUOUS / UNKNOWN). A hint only: identity and
live data still come from the asset's QR marker. Run on request, not per frame; nothing is stored.

get.description: What the browser can use: local STT / TTS, or none (then the mic is hidden, answers use the browser voice).
Unauthenticated liveness probe for Docker. Reveals nothing sensitive.

AssetInspect.title: AssetInspect
AssetInspect.description: A recorded inspection: when, what was found, when the next is due.

AssetMaintenanceRow.title: AssetMaintenanceRow
AssetMaintenanceRow.description: One line of an equipment's maintenance history. No reporter identity.

BookingEquipment.title: BookingEquipment
BookingEquipment.description: Chosen in the booking step 'Equipment'. Empty everywhere = none needed.

BookingSlot.title: BookingSlot
BookingSlot.description: A reserved interval. Identity only for staff or for the booking's owner.

IssuePhotoStage.title: IssuePhotoStage
IssuePhotoStage.description: When a photo was taken. Maintenance photos never replace report ones.

IssueUpdate.title: IssueUpdate
IssueUpdate.description: Staff edits. Status changes go through the status endpoint.

LabIssueBrief.title: LabIssueBrief
LabIssueBrief.description: What anyone may see about a lab's open problems: no reporter, no text.

LabOverview.title: LabOverview
LabOverview.description: One row per lab for the catalogue: everything a card shows, one query.

LifecycleEntry.title: LifecycleEntry
LifecycleEntry.description: One line of an item's life: reported, fixed, inspected, lent, moved.

PhotoReview.title: PhotoReview
PhotoReview.description:
One decision per photo, in the order sent (owner 2026-10-20): accept = use it (staff vouch;
the face server must still find a face) | refuse = never use it | retake = not used, ask for a new
one | auto = "skip": the system decides with the same check as at upload - used only when the face
server sees a face that is this account holder (or nobody registered), dropped otherwise.

SessionEndReason.title: SessionEndReason
SessionEndReason.description:
Why an occupancy session stopped counting. Only EXIT_RECORDED means an
exit was actually observed; every other value is the system admitting it
does not know when the person left, and the UI must say so.

SessionOut.title: SessionOut
SessionOut.description:
One occupancy span - when somebody was actually inside the room.

Distinct from a booking: a booking is an intention, a session is evidence.

SessionTrace.title: SessionTrace
SessionTrace.description: One occupancy session, traced: who, where, both factors, the door.

SignupRequest.title: SignupRequest
SignupRequest.description:
Public sign-up. No role and no auth_subject: always a plain student. A username
(firstname.lastname) is required for new accounts (owner, 2026-10-20).

TraceSummary.title: TraceSummary
TraceSummary.description: The one-screen answer to 'what happened with this booking at the door'.
